claims: Ramadan is the holiest month in the Islamic calendar.
During Ramadan, Muslims abstain from food, drink, smoking, and negative behaviors from dawn to sunset.
Ramadan marks when the Quran was first revealed to Prophet Muhammad.
Healthy adult Muslims fast daily from dawn (Fajr) to sunset (Maghrib) during Ramadan.
Exemptions from fasting apply to children, the elderly, the sick, pregnant/breastfeeding individuals, and travelers during Ramadan.
During Ramadan, meals are eaten before dawn (suhoor) and after sunset (iftar).
Tarawih prayers are held at night in mosques during Ramadan.
The main goal of Ramadan is to develop taqwa (God-consciousness or spiritual discipline).
Ramadan ends with the celebration of Eid al-Fitr.
